title: First Word Starting With the Search Term
statement:
You get a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces, and a lowercase term.

Return the 1-based position of the first word that begins with term. If no word begins with it, return -1.

examples.why: "bread" is word 3. "bravely" also starts with "br" but not with "bre".
Words 1, 2 and 3 all start with "go". Return the first.
"cat" and "sat" contain "at", but not at their start.

constraints: sentence has no leading or trailing spaces and single spaces between words
hints: Split the sentence into words, remembering that positions start at 1.
A word qualifies only if term matches at its very first character.
Without splitting: walk the sentence, and at each word start (index 0 or just after a space) compare term character by character, counting words as you go.

explain.intuition:
Split the sentence and test each word with a prefix check, returning the first match. The only decisions are using a prefix test rather than a contains test, and returning a 1-based position.

Splitting builds an array of every word. A single pass with an index avoids that: track where each word starts, compare term from there, and stop at the first success. It is the same idea as a cursor scanning text without tokenising it first.
steps: Keep a word counter starting at 1 and an index i at the start of the current word.
Compare term with the characters starting at i, stopping at a mismatch, a space or the end.
If all of term matched, return the counter.
Otherwise skip to the next space, step past it and increment the counter. Return -1 after the last word.
pitfalls: Checking includes instead of a prefix match, which accepts "cat" for "at".
Letting the comparison run across a space into the next word, for example treating "a b" as starting with "a b". Terms have no spaces, but the scan still has to stop at the word's end.

complexity.space: O(1) for the scan, O(n) if you split

solutions.title: Split and check each word
solutions.idea: Split on spaces and return the first index whose word starts with term, plus one.

solutions.title: Single scan without splitting
solutions.idea: Walk the sentence once. At each word start, compare term in place; then jump past the next space.

followups: Return the positions of all matching words instead of the first.
Many different terms are queried against the same long sentence. What would you build once to answer each query fast?
lcTitle: Check If a Word Occurs As a Prefix of Any Word in a Sentence
